text: I don't like how redundant frames are taking valuable space of the phone screen on all momentum pages including the feed. I like the cards animation when I swipe left or right but the frame must be removed. The card can appear only on swipe. And all the frames from other pages must go.
Lists, panels, the answer box and the entity references are frameless on phone now. Next is the feed card itself.
Typecheck passes. Now checking it in Firefox at phone size.
Web build is done; now running a phone-sized Firefox check against mocked feed data.
Feed is good on both phone and desktop (desktop keeps its card stack). Settings rendered blank in my mock, so I'm checking why before I judge the lists.

I've removed the frames on phone screens. Wider screens like your laptop keep theirs.

**Feed** ([Feed screen](Frontend/Screen/feed))
- When the card is still, it has no border, rounded corners or shadow, and no stacked cards show behind it. The card fills the whole width under the counters.
- The card shows up only when you drag it. Its edge, corners and shadow fade in as you swipe left or right, or pull it up. The tilt, the APPROVE / REWORK / ASK stamps and the green or red background are unchanged.
- The chat on a card is now just a strip below a thin line, with no box around it.

**Other pages**
- **Settings, Explorer, Sessions and Timeline:** the lists have no outer box. Rows still have their dividers and now line up with the section headings, so you get about 30px more width.
- **Metrics:** the panels have no outer box.
- **Explorer:** the answer box and an entity's references have no outer box.
- **Sessions:** the agent activity line and the document an interview is writing have no outer box.

I kept the outlines on things that need them to be read or used: text fields, chat bubbles, buttons, toggles, tables, diagrams, the drop-down menus and the rework sheet.

The app type-checks. I checked it in Firefox at phone width with sample feed and settings data: the feed card at rest, mid-swipe and with the rework sheet open, plus Settings. I also looked at the feed and Settings at desktop width, which look the same as before. I didn't open Explorer, Sessions, Timeline or Metrics, and didn't run the end-to-end tests.

The feed card in the knowledge base still says "one on top, two behind". The summarization step that runs after this one should correct that.
